links.outcome: Model performance across four centers and diverse OCT devices in external and real-world validation
links.effect: External validation on 1345 patients across four different-tier centers and diverse OCT devices; real-world validation across centers showed stable performance (F1: 90.22–95.24%).
links.quote: Real-world validation across centers also showed stable performance (F1: 90.22–95.24%).

links.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with expert ophthalmologists on abnormality detection and multi-disease diagnosis
links.effect: FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), with better efficiency.
links.quote: In human-machine comparisons, FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), while demonstrating better efficiency.

unlisted_practices: Automated image quality assessment as a gate before AI diagnosis
Aggregation of 2D slice-level predictions into 3D patient-level diagnosis

screen.reason: The study develops and validates an end-to-end foundation-model diagnostic pipeline (FOCUS) for 3D OCT retinal disease detection, including multi-center external validation and human-machine comparison, but tests model performance rather than specific operational deployment practices or safeguards.
